## Why This Is Asked

- Per-record data contracts and type coercion
- Idempotent upserts via MERGE into Iceberg

USING staged_features AS s
ON t.tenant_id = s.tenant_id

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts

- Deduplication keys and idempotent upserts
- End-to-end data lineage (OpenLineage integration)
- Lightweight data quality checks and reprocessing guards
- Two-stream ingestion vs micro-batching in a lakehouse

## Code Example

```python
# PySpark sketch for dedup and upsert into Iceberg
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

src = spark.read.csv("s3://partner-bucket/feed-*.csv", header=True)
dedup = src.withColumn("dedup_id", F.sha2(F.concat_ws("||", F.col("user_id"), F.col("event_time"), F.col("event_type")), 256))
# simplistic merge into Iceberg facts (pseudo-API)
dedup.write.format("iceberg").option("merge.mode", "upsert").save("db.events")

# lineage would emit OpenLineage events at each stage
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world data ingestion at multi-tenant scale, privacy controls, and the trade-offs between MongoDB Change Streams and Debezium in a lakehouse context. It also probes idempotency, schema evolution, and end-to-end correctness under late data.

- Region/tenant isolation and stream partitioning
- Iceberg lakehouse upserts and tombstones

- Watermarking for late data and schema evolution strategies

## Code Example

```sql
-- Minimal MERGE example for Iceberg
MERGE INTO iceberg_table AS t
USING staged_changes AS s
ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'update' THEN UPDATE SET t.value = s.new_value
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'delete' THEN DELETE
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, value) VALUES (s.id, s.new_value);
```
